chunks: Saad narrated from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal from Amr ibn Sa'id from Musaddiq ibn Sadah from Ammar ibn Musa al-Sabati from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding a man who hears the prostration verse (in recitation) during the time when prayer is not valid, before sunset and after Fajr prayer, he said: 'He does not prostrate.'

And regarding a man who recites a surah containing one of the obligatory prostrations in the obligatory prayer, he said: 'When he reaches the place of prostration, let him not recite it; and if he wishes to return, let him recite another surah and leave the one containing the prostration, and return to the other.'

And regarding a man who prays behind a group but does not follow them, praying for himself, and they sometimes recite an obligatory prostration verse but do not prostrate in it, so what should he do? He said: 'He does not prostrate.'

key_terms.السَّجْدَةُ: Prostration (specifically the prostration due to reciting a Quranic verse)
key_terms.الْعَزَائِمُ: Obligatory prostrations (specific verses in the Quran that require prostration)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on prostrating for the Quranic verse when praying during times when prayer is not valid or when following a group that does not prostrate?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the jurisprudence of *Sajdat al-Tilawah* (prostration of recitation) by establishing that it is not obligatory during specific times of prayer invalidity or when following an Imam who omits it. It highlights the Shia scholarly principle of distinguishing between the act of recitation and the act of prostration, allowing flexibility for the worshipper to skip the verse entirely or simply omit the prostration while continuing the prayer.
